sentences: **Narrowing to f16 uses integer ops, not `PackHalf2x16`.** Every f16 ALU result (`v_*_f16` VOP1/VOP2/VOP3, `v_pk_*_f16`, `v_cvt_f16_f32`, `v_interp_p2_f16`, `v_fma_mix*`) and `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32` go through `Gen.f16_bits` (round to nearest even, or round toward zero for pkrtz; f16 denormals kept, f32 denormal inputs give ±0, NaN stays a quiet NaN).
After a MODE.FP_ROUND toward-zero write the ALU results take the toward-zero form instead (`Gen.f16_res`; see Known approximations).

GLSL.std.450 leaves `PackHalf2x16`'s rounding to the implementation, and drivers fold a `PackHalf2x16` → `UnpackHalf2x16` round trip to a no-op, so the next f16 op saw the unrounded f32: #513 (RTX 6000 Ada, `--wave64-emulate`, `v_pk_add_f16` → `v_pk_mul_f16` 1 ulp off), and pkrtz giving round-to-nearest on llvmpipe.
**f16 FMAs round once** (`v_fma_f16`, `v_fmac_f16`, `v_pk_fma_f16`): x·y is exact in f32, TwoSum gives the exact error of the f32 sum, and round-to-odd at f32 then rounds correctly to f16.
An RX 6700 matched a correctly rounded f16 FMA in 12,612 of 12,612 cases (#374); `Fma` then narrowing double-rounded.

Checked by `tests/semantic/test_f16_int_convert.py` (edges + seeded sweep against Python's binary16), `tests/semantic/test_f16_fma_rounding.py` (exact rational reference; built near-tie cases fail on the old translation) and `tools/valu_fuzz.py --family f16` on an RTX 6000 Ada.
Image/buffer d16 packing (#489) and the 16-bit interpolant quantize (#512) are separate.

**Widening an f16 ALU operand doesn't trust `UnpackHalf2x16` with denormals** (`Gen.f16_in`): on an RTX 5060 Ti (610.88) it gives 0 for a denormal that an SDWA `BYTE_1` select produced, from an inline constant or a VGPR alike, while the same denormal as a literal or already in a VGPR widens right (a local probe of all four, before and after).
So a half whose exponent field is 0 is widened as sign × mantissa × 2^-24 with integer ops.

Confirmed by the GPU test `ps_sdwa_f16_const` (word y, the denormal `0x0040` × 1024.0 = `0x1c00`), which gave `0x0000` on an RTX 5060 Ti (610.88) natively and under `--wave64-emulate` before and 4096/4096 exact after, and by `tests/semantic/test_value_semantics.py` running it with a flushing `UnpackHalf2x16`.
The other `UnpackHalf2x16` uses (packed-f16 reads, interpolants, d16 image results) are not changed.

`v_fma_mix*` with f32 sources rounds once straight to f16 via round-to-odd in both nearest and toward-zero modes (measured on an RDNA2 iGPU, gfx1036: `tools/fma_mix_probe.py --oracle hw` gave the single-rounded word for all 7 of 7 tie inputs where the two rules differ, SHADER-135; see Known approximations).

`v_fma_mix*` rounds once straight to f16 via round-to-odd in both nearest-even and toward-zero modes, matching hardware (7 of 7 tie inputs of `tools/fma_mix_probe.py --oracle hw` on gfx1036, SHADER-135; see Known approximations).

`v_fma_mix*` rounds once straight to f16 via round-to-odd in both nearest and toward-zero modes (see Known approximations); the hardware rounds once: 7 of 7 tie inputs of `tools/fma_mix_probe.py --oracle hw` on gfx1036 (SHADER-135).

`v_fma_mix*` with f32 sources uses `Fma` then narrows (two roundings, unmeasured) in nearest-even mode; toward zero it rounds once (see Known approximations). 7 of 7 tie inputs of `tools/fma_mix_probe.py --oracle hw` on gfx1036 (SHADER-135; not fixed yet); toward zero it rounds once (see Known approximations).
